title: AlignCanvas: browser tool turning images into 3D motion
author: Basit A. Khan
text:
Everything I’ve posted lately was made with a tool I’ve been quietly building.

Today it’s public: aligncanvas.com beta is live.

Turn your images into 3D motion in a few clicks. Nothing to install, and your images never leave your device. It all runs in your browser.

why: Pale, near-monochrome card UI with soft blurs and a single big percentage: same Little Plains calm as the radar chart he approved.

why: A pale sage dropper bottle with a fine orbit line around the cap: restrained 3D packaging motion with almost no colour.

why: A black radial dial interface with thin rings and small labels: a monochrome take on the circular UI he keeps approving.

why: A dark interactive card holding a glassy 3D prism, built as a remixable Spline file: the Spline product-card format he approved.
author: splinetool

why: A frosted glass toggle with a plus sign on soft grey: a 3D take on a single UI control, close to the Spline product card he approved.

title: Exploded chrome mechanism
why: Chrome parts drifting apart against black in slow motion: precise, monochrome 3D product animation.
author: romenkaelin

title: Mouthwash motion study 16
why: A field of short white strokes turning like iron filings on black, from Mouthwash Studio's research index: calm creative coding in monochrome.
author: Mouthwash Studio

title: ElevenLabs brand updates, work in progress
why: A first look at updates to the ElevenLabs brand by @marinaanddesign with @dariaiareshko and @victoiredouy: black-and-white layouts with soft blue imagery, shown in motion.
author: @marinaanddesign

title: Monotree feature sections UI, Oleksandr Plyuto
why: White feature cards with toggles, a schedule picker and checklist states on pale grey: clean product UI motion like the Alembic tool UI he approved.
author: Oleksandr Plyuto

title: Netfacade brand guidelines
why: Guidelines pages for Netfacade by Abigail Natucci: Archivo type specimen, greys and one orange, laid out on a strict grid.
author: Abigail Natucci

title: Line ribbon study, Matthias Meissen
why: A generative ribbon of fine white lines folding on black, by Matthias Meissen: calm monochrome creative coding.
author: matthiasmeissen

title: Ribbed cosmetic bottle render
why: A slow close-up of a ribbed, pale cosmetic bottle with water droplets: quiet 3D packaging motion, close to the DOJOLIQ render he approved this morning.
author: Roman (via superdesigners.co)

title: Paul Kalkbrenner website, Holographik
why: Holographik's website for Paul Kalkbrenner: a minimal black-and-white layout with crafted animations and interactions.
author: Holographik (holographik.co)

title: AMS identity, Advanced Micro Systems
why: Black-and-white posters with a bold geometric mark and quiet grotesk headlines: a calm, monochrome identity system.
author: dominikkorolczu (Behance)

title: UI generation skeleton effect
author: Jakub Antalik
text:
Created a new skill for UI generation skeleton effect, something I’ve been using in my UI videos.

These UI examples are built with transitions.dev UI Agent.

title: Buttons with Feelings, aleksksaa
why: Plain white buttons that react with tiny faces as you hover and press: one clever, warm idea in a near-monochrome UI.
author: @aleksksaa (via recent.design)

title: Depth Animation, hal_chemy
why: A sphere of white points on black turning in depth: refined monochrome generative motion.
author: @hal_chemy (via bestdesignsonx)

title: Radial menu interaction, pxdx studio
why: A black asterisk button that blooms into a cluster of grey menu bubbles with counters: one clever interaction, close to the Ope radial dial he approved.
author: pxdxstudio

title: Transparent device housing
why: A clear-cased gadget showing its dark internals on white, a crafted product object in the transparent-hardware vein.
author: unknown (Instagram)

title: Threaded device render, Studio Tendril
why: A clear device drawn out of a field of fine threads that settles into a solid object, a material idea in motion rather than another loop.
author: studiotendril

title: Machined joint close-up, werk.core
why: A machined metal joint and button in soft grey light with a tiny red indicator, crafted hardware detail in the same vein as his 3D approvals.
author: werk.core

title: Patch identity system
why: A black-and-white identity for Patch shown as a moving system: modular mark, grid and interface pages working together.
author: Patch (via recent.design)

title: Black glass hinge render, orlov.it
why: A glossy black glass hinge, like an eyewear frame, turning in grey light: the same material-led 3D close-up as the exploded chrome mechanism he approved.
author: orlov.it

title: Dark radial dial tool UI
why: A quiet dark tool where a step list on the left drives a large tick-marked dial, a cousin of the Ope radial dial; creator not credited on Cosmos.
author: unknown

title: Laptop internals macro, Vinícius Araújo
why: A slow macro pass through a laptop's keyboard and inner parts in black and silver, close to the exploded chrome mechanism he approved.
author: va_viniciusaraujo

title: Tempo identity motion, Studio Dumbar
why: Part of Studio Dumbar's full identity for the Tempo payments network: white lanes that stretch and travel on black, built with custom motion software.
author: Studio Dumbar/DEPT

title: Age progression slider, Adi
why: A minimal web UI where one slider ages a portrait from child to old age, product UI that does one clever thing.
author: Adi (via recent.design)

title: The Gucci Twinsburg Fashion Show
author: GUCCI
text: Gucci Spring Summer 2023 at Milan Fashion Week (Alessandro Michele): one collection shown across two mirrored runways, walked by pairs of identical twins.

title: Study Hall website clock
why: Study Hall's new site opens on a minimal analogue clock face in black and white, one simple and well-made idea.
author: studyhall.design

title: Cyphr, Holographik
why: Holographik's Cyphr project: grainy black-and-white photography with big numbered sections, from the studio behind the Kalkbrenner site he approved.
author: Holographik

title: Halo Industries identity timer, iamcollaps
why: Part of the Halo Industries identity: a radial tick dial counting up around a black dot, close to the dial UIs he keeps approving.
author: iamcollaps

title: Wireframe wave over dot planes
why: A white wireframe surface rippling above stacked dot grids on black, refined monochrome generative motion like the Meissen line studies.
author: unknown (saved by khuan on Cosmos)

title: Weight picker dial
why: A weight picker where the numbers roll over a ruler of ticks as you drag, a single dial interaction done cleanly.
author: kirschberg

title: Walkman, Tektura Studio
why: A clear-cased Walkman with its tape mechanism on show, close to the transparent device housing and Studio Tendril pieces he approved.
author: tekturastudio

title: Devouring Details radial index
why: The intro to the Devouring Details site lays its chapters out on a tick-marked dial you scrub around, a quiet radial UI in the vein of the pxdx menu and Ope dial he approved.
author: tylerj

title: Radial line field, samdape
why: Thin white lines sweep around a dark dial face in a loop, a refined generative clock study like the wireframe wave he approved.
author: samdape

title: Tech Central identity, For The People
why: Chunky cut-out numerals carry a whole precinct identity, from bus shelters to black-and-white typographic panels. It's a full system shown in use.
author: For The People

title: Forward by Tatari identity, A LINE
why: A LINE's identity for the Forward forum uses big black, white and green pixel blocks that crop portraits, shown on street posters at full scale.
author: A LINE

title: Nothing Phone (4a) and Headphone (a) R&D, Future Deluxe
why: Future Deluxe's R&D film for Nothing moves through grey and black close-ups of camera rings, glyph lights and headphone curves, focused on materials rather than a product pitch.
author: Future Deluxe (via HERE CREATIVE)

title: Event ticket pass purchase confirmation
why: A lanyard-style event ticket swings in beside a calm confirmation screen, then the flow moves on to adding it to your calendar. A direct reference for how an agent could show a ticket it just bought.
author: Unknown (via uitopic)

title: Kinetic installation, FUN AND AWE
why: Thousands of black and white balls in a tall white box tumble and settle into shifting wave patterns. A real object in motion, entirely monochrome.
author: FUN AND AWE (via zhestkov)

title: Copilot icon motion states, Microsoft Design
why: Copilot's two-square mark moves differently for Thinking, Planning and Retrieval, so the icon itself shows what the assistant is doing. One clever idea in product UI, in black on white.
author: Microsoft Design with COLLINS and Koto

title: INVERSE kinetic sculpture, Christopher Bauder
why: Hundreds of black spheres on fine cables rise and fall as one slow wave against a bright window in a concrete room. A real object in motion, almost entirely black and white.
author: Christopher Bauder (via darkmatterberlin)

title: Chiba Tech identity, Giorgia Lupi / Pentagram
why: A bold black-and-white mark built from stripes and checks, shown on a projecting street sign, a phone case and a happi coat. A full identity system applied in real use, like Tech Central and Forward.
author: Giorgia Lupi and team at Pentagram

title: Flight status card animation
why: A small JFK-to-LAX card zooms in so the plane icon flies along an ON TIME progress line, then settles back. A ticket-style status object, useful for the cinema-ticket demo.
author: Unknown (spotted by Best Designs on X)

title: Wav.Disort identity, Hrvoje Grubisic of HOLOGRAPHIK
why: A grey-and-white identity for an experimental sound event in Atlanta, where radial sound-wave rings and big dates run across posters and a site. Holographik is a studio he already trusts.
author: HOLOGRAPHIK (Hrvoje Grubisic)

title: Culture House Sunderland identity, Studio Blackburn
why: Studio Blackburn's Culture House Sunderland identity builds one chunky house-shaped CH mark and carries it onto business cards, numbered wayfinding signs and posters. A full system shown in use, like Tech Central.
author: studioblackburn

title: Nike Gangnam installation, creative direction Benjamin Kaplan
why: Black pill shapes on a white wall tumble, stack into columns and scatter as a man walks past and pushes a big black disc. Pure black and white, one playful physical idea.
author: Benjamin Kaplan (creative direction)

title: 3.11LABS x Lacoste graphics, HOLOGRAPHIK
why: A long black board of thin white technical graphics, labels and small icons for 3.11LABS and Lacoste. From Holographik, whose Wav.Disort you just kept.
author: HOLOGRAPHIK and 3.11LABS (via interfaceindex)

title: National Museum of Ireland identity, Zero-G
why: Zero-G's identity for the National Museum of Ireland, with a custom Altform typeface from CoType, shown on street posters, a billboard and a Collins Barracks map. An applied system on your own streets.
author: Zero-G Studio (via cotypefoundry)

title: 3D card payment animation, Airbnb iOS app
why: While it says 'Reviewing payment details', a small 3D card reader with a flower on it sits on a white screen, then it lands on 'Your reservation is confirmed!'. A calm Airbnb-style payment state for the agent.
author: Airbnb (via 60fps.design)

title: The Park Kraków wayfinding, Blank Studio
why: Black-and-white wayfinding for The Park Kraków office complex: big numerals on striped walls, black pylons and bilingual 'Cześć / Hello' wall type. An applied system in a real building.
author: Blank Studio

title: Plasma card activation, the card becomes the form
why: In Plasma's app the silver card itself flips into the activation and PIN form instead of sitting above a generic form. A shipped, monochrome card moment that fits the agent app's disposable cards.
author: Plasma (via 60fps.design)

title: Holographik 'The story of a Family' type motion
why: Image-filled headline type on a plain page; calm editorial motion.
author: holographik.co

title: Balenciaga for Numéro 213, Sebastian Kim
why: Edita Vilkeviciute in black Balenciaga on a rocky shoreline, shot in high-contrast black and white.
author: Sebastian Kim

title: ARC Radio / Under Coffee poster
why: Black poster with grey type running vertically up the middle, framed by tiny catalogue-style text blocks.

title: NOCTA sale campaign, Melody Digital
why: Black campaign layout with tight Swiss type, a huge white Swoosh and one grainy black-and-white photo.
author: Melody Digital

title: CRED cashback animation
why: Shipped reward moment in the CRED app: streaks of light rush past before the cashback amount lands.
author: CRED

title: Cleaver Keyboard, Serene Industries
why: A keyboard machined from one aluminium block, with pill-shaped keys and engraved legends.
author: Serene Industries

title: typetype poster
why: Black-and-white poster: a full bleed of dark sea with the foundry's name set big along the bottom edge.
author: typetype

title: Velvet armchair with oranges, Guilherme Wentz
why: Warm, single-colour still life of a rounded velvet chair with three oranges tucked into its arm.
author: Guilherme Wentz

title: Linear UI interaction, Emil Kowalski
why: A small, precise interaction study for Linear's interface by Emil Kowalski.
author: emilkowalski

title: PALO engraved monogram plate
why: A stacked serif PALO monogram engraved into a brushed metal plate, shot flat on deep brown.

title: Radial marks, blankenship
why: Two circular marks made of radiating bars, one twisting into an eye, set in black and white.
author: blankenship

title: SingleStore identity, Standard Projects
why: An identity built on time-based logic, carried into a stark grey product UI with huge numerals.
author: Standard Projects

title: Magnolia Central Park, Ortica Studio
why: Black-and-white type poster with the name set huge and vertical against faint construction lines.
author: Ortica Studio

title: Red dress in a fog-filled bowl
why: A figure in a red knit dress lies in a white concrete bowl filled with low fog.

title: Nochmal poster, Ellen Hitzer, 2011
why: Huge cropped black-and-white letterforms stacked into a dense, rhythmic poster.
author: Ellen Hitzer

title: Beaux Arts Ball 2025 identity, Eddie Opara at Pentagram
why: An identity themed Pattern Recognition, built from heavy black glyph-like shapes and scattered characters.
author: Eddie Opara, Pentagram

title: Eddy sticker pack, designbyaron
why: A sticker-pack opening interaction where a crinkled orange foil packet tears open to reveal the stickers.
author: designbyaron

title: Last train to nowhere
why: Dusk film still of a lit train on the shoreline, watched from a cliff; cinematic and quiet.

title: The Creative Compass manual, CAPSLOCK
why: Swiss-style black-and-white manual spread with a huge grotesk headline split across the gutter.
author: CAPSLOCK

title: Suited magazine spread, New Studio
why: Split-word headline set huge in serif against black-and-white fashion photography.
author: New Studio

title: Editorial web motion, Aristide Benoist
why: Grey, quiet website motion with a dancer and tiny UI chrome; very restrained craft.
author: Aristide Benoist

title: Naver Pay Media Day 2025
why: Yu Jaewan's black-and-white system for Naver Pay's media day: a white key-visual panel over a rotating sphere of type, carried from naming through keynote and motion.
author: Yu Jaewan

title: MOLG GEN2 robotic installation
why: A black-and-white robotic installation: a steel rig of arms holding a black screen of white type against a white wall.
author: MOLG

title: Nike Rise, generative visual centre
why: FIELD's generative system for Nike Rise stores: live data turned into motion across the retail space.
author: FIELD

title: Open Season 2026 identity
why: Kristian S at Design Bigfish gave Brisbane's winter music and art programme a sports-energy identity, with a blurred black OS26 on flat signal orange.
author: Kristian S / Design Bigfish

title: Aesop, Seven Rooms, Tokyo
why: Aesop's 'poetry of the everyday' installation in Tokyo: warm timber rooms lined with shelves and lived-in objects.
author: Aesop

title: Authors Roman revival poster
why: Black poster for Jahn Koutrios's Authors Roman revival at ECAL: stacked bracketed numbers in a crisp serif with a dense column of small type.
author: Jahn Koutrios (ECAL)

title: Infinity 8.0
why: Jules Langeard's black-and-white aerial film looking straight down into a curved, figure-eight concrete form.
author: Jules Langeard

title: Hair painting
why: Barber Mohammad Hamze cuts and paints a layered blue-and-orange pattern into a close crop, shot straight from behind on white.
author: Mohammad Hamze

title: Emerging Designers & Second Hand Archive Sales poster
why: Black-and-white event poster: tight condensed caps on top and a winding road of grainy photo snaking down the page.

title: Aave Pro: delightful transaction states
author: Abhijeet Singh
text: Delightful transaction states in Aave Pro ✨

title: Copenhagen Half Marathon identity
why: Norgram's identity for the race, animated by Relay Studio: flat orange blocks, a stride-like mark and big grotesk type cut against grainy black-and-white crowd photography.
author: Norgram, motion by Relay Studio

title: Alva Noto + Ryuichi Sakamoto, Revep
why: The Revep 12-inch pressed on clear vinyl with a plain white label, as quiet and exact as the music.
author: Alva Noto + Ryuichi Sakamoto (Raster-Noton)

title: Skullet: smart skeleton loading states
author: Lochie Axon
text: Skullet has no additional build step, reveal transitions and skeleton stylings are fully customisable, SSR content shows right away with no loading state flash… https://skullet.lochie.me

author: Liron Eldar-Ash (LIŔONA) / BUCK

text: Ghostly: typography, color, iconography, motion, data viz, backgrounds, two illustration styles and 3D. BUCK team with Aave Labs (Alex Vanderzon, Paris Rouzati, Lochie Axon, et al.). Also: https://www.rebrand.gallery/bento/aave

title: The Lives They Lived, The New York Times Magazine
why: The magazine's annual memorial issue paced as a flip-through: big stacked condensed caps for each name, then spreads of archive photos and objects.
author: Gail Bichler, The New York Times Magazine

title: Summer at Mezzatorre, Ischia
